179	**Merging several branches cut from the same commit conflicts in
180	`docs/backlog.md`.** Every fix inserts its entry at the top of §1.1, so the
181	second and third merges land on the same anchor. The resolution is always to
182	keep both sides — they are independent entries, not competing edits.
183	
184	### Landing a sandbox-made commit (host-relay)
185	
186	A Docker Sandbox (`sbx`) has no `entire://` auth of its own — `ENTIRE_TOKEN`
187	via `sbx secret set-custom` doesn't work (`git-remote-entire` parses the
188	JWT's claims locally, before any network call, but the secret proxy only
189	substitutes the real token on the wire — the sandbox process itself only
190	ever sees an unparseable placeholder), and an interactive `entire login`
191	inside the sandbox trades that for a persistent, harder-to-reason-about
192	credential sitting in a less-trusted place. So the sandbox edits and commits
193	locally only; the host does every `origin` operation — fetch, push, PR,
194	merge. `git pull`/`git fetch` run *inside* the sandbox will fail with `no
195	auth context for cluster ...` — that's expected, not a setup bug; don't
196	`entire login` there to fix it (see `~/projects/github/anthnel/sbx-kits/entire/README.md`
197	for the full rationale).
198	
199	A direct-mode sandbox mounts this exact repo directory, so its commits land
200	straight in the shared `.git` — the host sees them immediately, no transfer
201	needed. But `git worktree add -b <branch> ../devdesk-<branch> ...` run
202	*inside* the sandbox creates that sibling path **outside** the single
203	mounted directory, so it lands in the sandbox's own private container
204	layer — invisible to the host (`git worktree list` shows it `prunable`).
205	The commit object itself is still in the shared `.git/objects` though, so
206	nothing is actually lost:
207	
208	```bash
209	# From the host, once the sandbox reports "done and committed":
210	git worktree list                      # confirm the sibling worktree, prunable, HEAD sha
211	git cat-file -t <sha>                  # confirm the commit is really in this .git (it is)
212	git worktree prune -v                  # drop the stale, unreachable admin entry
213	
214	git push origin <sha>:refs/heads/<branch>
215	gh pr create -R anthnel/devdesk --base main --head <branch> \
216	  --title "<subject line>" --body "$(git show -s --format=%b <sha>)"
217	gh pr merge -R anthnel/devdesk <n> --squash --delete-branch
218	git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main   # may need a retry, see above
219	```
220	
221	**A follow-up commit on the same branch, after the first one already got
222	squash-merged, will conflict on a plain `git merge`** — squashing rewrites
223	history, so `git merge origin/main` computes the wrong common ancestor
224	(the branch's *own* pre-squash parent) and re-diffs files that already
225	landed, even when nothing actually conflicts in substance. Don't hand-edit
226	through that; cherry-pick the new commit straight onto current `origin/main`
227	instead — its real parent already matches what's on `main`, so it applies
228	clean:
229	
230	```bash
231	git worktree add -b <tmp-branch> ../devdesk-<tmp-branch> <new-sha>
232	cd ../devdesk-<tmp-branch>
233	git reset --hard origin/main
234	git cherry-pick <new-sha>              # clean apply — verify before trusting this
235	go build ./... && go test ./<touched-packages>/...
236	git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch-name>
237	# gh pr create / gh pr merge as above, then from the main checkout:
238	git worktree remove ../devdesk-<tmp-branch>
239	```

- entire: Drive the Entire CLI (entire) for checkpoints, agent sessions, code provenance, and multi-agent review. Use when the user mentions Entire, checkpoints, session tracking, "entire why/blame/experts", agent activity recaps, or when a repo contains .entire/ and you need to inspect or manage tracked agent work.
- golang-patterns: Idiomatic Go patterns, best practices, and conventions for building robust, efficient, and maintainable Go applications. Use when writing or reviewing Go code and idiomatic structure or conventions are in question.
- golang-testing: Go testing patterns including table-driven tests, subtests, benchmarks, fuzzing, and test coverage. Follows TDD methodology with idiomatic Go practices. Use when writing Go tests — table-driven cases, subtests, benchmarks, fuzzing, or coverage.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

input.prompt:
The user asked: "est-ce que des fichiers plan ou des entrées dans le backlog doivent être nettoyées" (should any plan files or backlog entries be cleaned up).

Context: this is the devdesk repo (/c/Users/anthoni/projects/entire/anthnel/devdesk). Plans live in .claude/plans/*.md (44 files, ls output already gathered — oldest dated May 20, newest Aug 29). Per .claude/rules/planning.md, plans are meant to be implementation plans; design decisions that outlive a plan go to docs/backlog.md instead. Recent commit history (already fetched, last 20) shows features landing referencing §3.5x/§3.6x sections and D-numbered defects — these look like they trace back to docs/backlog.md entries.

Your job (investigate only, do NOT edit/delete anything — this is a report task):

1. Read docs/backlog.md in full. Understand its structure (sections like §1.1, §3.x, D-numbers for defects).
2. For each file in .claude/plans/, determine whether the plan appears to be FULLY IMPLEMENTED (i.e., the feature it describes is shipped in the current codebase / referenced as done in backlog.md or git log) vs still open/relevant. Cheap heuristic: match plan filename/topic against backlog.md §-section titles and against `git log --oneline -100` subjects; also spot-check a few plans by reading their first ~30 lines (they often have a status header or checklist) and briefly grepping whether the described files/feature exist in the codebase now.
3. For docs/backlog.md itself: check if it has stale entries — items marked done that should have been archived/removed, or defects (D-numbers) that are already fixed per git log (e.g. D68, D69, D67, D66, D65, D64, D62, D63, D59 all appear fixed in recent commits) but might still be listed as open in backlog.md. Check if there's an archival convention already in place (e.g. a "done" section vs "open" section) and whether it's being followed.
4. Do NOT read all 44 plan files in full — that would blow context. For most, a filename + one grep/date check is enough. Only Read fully the ones that are ambiguous (recent dates, or topics not obviously matched in git log).

Report back (under 400 words):
- A verdict: does backlog.md need cleanup, and which specific entries (with §/D numbers)?
- A list of plan files in .claude/plans/ that look safe to delete because fully shipped (be conservative — only list ones you're fairly confident about), grouped roughly by evidence used.
- Any plans that look ambiguous/worth a human look rather than auto-cleanup.
- Do not make changes. Just report findings so the user can decide.

input.prompt:
In the devdesk repo (Go, Bubble Tea TUI), there's a "jobs registry" system (internal/jobs) introduced per backlog §3.58 ("un registre de travaux, et une seule chaîne de spinner"), which other features (workspace clone, security scans) use to register long-running operations, track their status, and drive one shared spinner across the app plus a dedicated `:jobs` view. There's also a "K" key to stop a running job/target (§3.58 poste 8), and "le clone devient un run du registre" (§3.58 poste 7 — cloning a repo registers a job).

I need a thorough understanding of this system so I can plan a new feature: when a user pulls a Docker image from the OCI registry browser (the `G` key, calling `pullSelectedTag` in internal/ui/oci_resources/browser_tags.go which triggers `pullRegistryImageCmd` in internal/ui/oci_resources/commands.go, which calls `docker.PullImage`), that pull should register as a job in this registry (like clone does), and the OCI images view (internal/ui/oci_resources, the images table/list, separate from the registry browser) should show a spinner on the row for the image currently being pulled.

Please investigate and report back (be thorough, this feeds an implementation plan):

1. **internal/jobs package**: What's the core API? (e.g. how do you register a job — is there a `Start`/`Register` function, what fields does a Job have — target ID/name, kind/type, status, cancel func? How is job completion/failure signaled? How is the job registry queried — e.g. "is target X currently running a job of kind Y"?)

2. **How workspace clone integrates with it** (§3.58 poste 7, likely `internal/ui/workspaces` or similar) — find the actual code that calls into internal/jobs when a clone starts, how it reports progress/completion back to the clone's Bubble Tea model, and how the workspaces view then shows a per-row spinner for "cloning". This is the closest existing precedent for the OCI pull feature — trace it end to end (start job → Cmd → Msg → Update → View spinner rendering) with file:line references.

3. **How security scans integrate with it** similarly, if the pattern differs meaningfully from clone (e.g. because a scan can happen in oci_resources/images.go itself, which is architecturally closer to where the pull spinner needs to live).

4. **The `K` key / stop-a-run mechanism** (§3.58 poste 8) — how a running job for a specific target gets cancelled, in case pull should support this too (not necessarily required, just note if the pattern makes it "free").

5. **The `:jobs` view and the shared spinner chain** — how a job's spinner frame gets pushed/driven, and whether registering a job automatically makes it show up in `:jobs` and drive the global spinner, or if views need extra wiring.

6. **internal/ui/oci_resources package structure** — specifically the images view/table (as opposed to the registry browser we already know about): what file(s) render it, what message types exist for image state changes (e.g. is there already a "scanning" flag per row model similar to tagRow.scanning we saw in browser_tags.go?), and what Docker image list refresh mechanism exists (e.g. does docker.ListImages get called on some poll/refresh, and would a freshly-pulled image just show up after a refresh, or does something else need to update the list).

Report file:line references throughout so a plan can cite them precisely. Keep total report under 700 words but include all the concrete API signatures and file paths needed.

input.prompt:
In the devdesk repo (Go, Bubble Tea TUI), package internal/ui/oci_resources, I need to understand the "images" view/table (distinct from the registry browser in browser_*.go files) — this is the view that lists local Docker images (via internal/oci or internal/docker), reachable presumably via a shortcut like `:oci` or a tab in the OCI resources view.

I'm planning a feature where pulling an image from the registry browser (the `G` key) should show a spinner on the corresponding row in this images table while the pull is in progress, similar to how the security-scan spinner works per row (see internal/ui/oci_resources/browser_tags.go's tagRow struct which has `scanning bool` and `frame string` fields, and internal/ui/oci_resources/browser_view.go's rebuildTagTable() which sets those fields using `b.scanningTags[imageName]` and `spinner.Dot.Frames[b.tagScanSpinnerIdx%len(spinner.Dot.Frames)]`).

Please investigate and report back (this feeds an implementation plan, be thorough with file:line references):

1. Where is the images view/model defined? What file(s)? What's the top-level struct (e.g. `Model` or similar) that holds the list of Docker images, and what's the row/item type used in its datatable (per project convention `internal/ui/datatable`, see Rule 116/122/139 in project rules — cell text must stay plain, `Style` supplies color)?

2. How does this images view currently refresh its list of Docker images — is there a Cmd that calls into internal/docker or internal/oci to list images, on what trigger (key press, tick, on view load)? What Msg type carries the result back to Update()?

3. Is there ALREADY a per-row "busy"/spinner concept in this view (e.g. for image deletion, or scanning) that the pull spinner could follow as a template? Look for scan-related spinner state in the images view specifically (not the registry browser) — e.g. grep for `spinner`, `scanning`, `busy` in internal/ui/oci_resources/*.go excluding browser_*.go files. There's a project rule (Rule 139) that a datatable body must never be replaced by a spinner/message — the spinner must be a per-row visual, likely via a Style callback coloring/prefixing a status icon, consistent with Rule 122 (Cell returns plain text, Style colors it) and Rule 121 (circular status icons).

4. How would a freshly pulled image (via `docker pull`) become visible in this images table — does the view need an explicit refresh trigger after pull completes, or does it already re-list on some interval/focus event? Find the actual refresh Cmd/function.

5. What message-passing path exists (if any) between the registry browser sub-model and the parent oci_resources model/images view — i.e. when the browser is closed or a pull happens, does a Msg propagate up to the parent Model that could be intercepted to mark an image row as "pulling" and later refresh the list? Look at the parent model's Update() switch and how it composes the registry browser vs the images view (likely internal/ui/oci_resources/model.go or view.go).

Report file:line references throughout. Keep total report under 700 words but include concrete type/field names and signatures.

**2. Clone integration (§3.58 poste 7)** — `internal/ui/forge/explorer/clone.go`, `clone_jobs.go`, `clone_list.go`

End-to-end: `handleCloneDestinationSelected` (clone.go:84) builds an **open** run via `m.cloneJobRun(target)` → `jobs.NewOpenRun(jobs.KindClone, command.ViewGitExplorer, "", target)` (clone.go:125), then returns `jobs.StartCancellable(run, waitForCloneEvent(run.events), run.cancel)` (clone.go:117). Router's `handleStartJobs` (app/jobs.go:40) admits it via `a.jobs.Start(run)` and dispatches the work Cmd. Progress arrives as `CloneEventMsg`, which implements `Transition()` (clone_jobs.go:15) mapping clone-pipeline events to `jobs.ItemQueued/Running/Done/Skipped/Failed` with `Discover:true` for newly-found repos. `CloneRunFinishedMsg` implements `Seal() jobs.Kind` (clone_jobs.go:46). Router's `routeWork` (app/jobs.go:67) applies the transition/seal to the registry *before* forwarding to the view, then `jobsChanged()` broadcasts `jobs.ChangedMsg` to all views and (re)starts the shared tick. `handleJobsChanged` (clone.go:183) stores `m.jobs`/`m.jobFrame`, and if a clone list is open, `cloneRunFrom(msg.Runs)` (clone_list.go:225) picks the run and `l.setRun(run, frame)` (clone_list.go:167) stamps the shared frame onto `ItemRunning` rows only (`cloneRow.frame`), rendered as `frame + " cloning"` in `cloneStatusLabel` (clone_list.go:132). Cancel: `esc` → `jobs.CancelOpen(jobs.KindClone)` (clone.go:238).

**3. Security scans** (`security/jobs.go`) and **OCI image scans** (`oci_resources/jobs.go`) — the closer precedent for pull. Both use plain (non-open) `jobs.NewRun(jobs.KindScan, origin, "", label, names...)` (oci_resources/jobs.go:42, called from `scanSelectedImage` in images.go:68). `ImageScanStartingMsg`/`ImageScanFinishedMsg` implement `Transition()` (jobs.go:95-106) and are routed via `app.go:404-408`. `handleJobsChanged` (oci_resources/jobs.go:26) rebuilds `m.updateImageTable()` and pushes `scanningNames()` into the registry browser. Row-level flag: `scanningImage(name)` (jobs.go:57) queries `jobs.Unfinished(m.jobs)` for `KindScan` items matching the image name — this is the exact pattern to copy for `scanningPull(name)`/`KindPull`.

**4. `K` / stop-a-run** — Registry-side machinery (`Cancel`, `CancelItem`, `Run.Stoppable`, `Run.ItemStoppable`, `Kind.Cancellable`) is fully generic and already true for `KindPull`. But the **key binding itself is not free**: today `keymap.Kill` ("K") is only wired in `internal/ui/jobsview/update.go:113` (`stopSelected`, using `jobs.CancelItem(m.openRun, target)`) and a couple of unrelated views (containers, netdiag). Neither `oci_resources/images.go` nor `browser_tags.go`/`browser_keys.go` bind K to `jobs.CancelItem`/`jobs.Cancel` today — adding row-level stop for pull needs new key-handling code in oci_resources, though the registry logic (`Cancellable`, `CancelItem`) needs no changes.

**5. `:jobs` view / shared spinner** — Registering via `jobs.Start`/`StartCancellable` automatically shows up in `:jobs` (`jobsview/update.go` reads `msg.Runs` from the same `ChangedMsg` broadcast, no extra wiring) and automatically drives the shared spinner: `app/jobs.go:215` `ensureJobTick()` starts the one tick chain whenever `a.jobs.Running() > 0`, and `broadcastJobs()` (app/jobs.go:182) pushes `ChangedMsg` to *every* held view each tick. Views just need to store `msg.Frame`/`msg.Runs` in their own `handleJobsChanged`, and rebuild their row cache (`updateImageTable`, `refreshRows`, etc.) — that per-view wiring is what does need to be added, not the spinner chain itself.

**6. `internal/ui/oci_resources` images view structure**

- `internal/ui/oci_resources/table.go`: `imageRow` struct (table.go:27-36) has `Image docker.Image`, `DisplayName`, `RawName`, `Entry cache.ImageScanEntry`, `Scanned`, `Scanning bool`, `Failed`, `SpinnerFrame string` — i.e. there is already a `Scanning` flag analogous to `tagRow.scanning`, driven by `m.scanningNames()` inside `imageRows()` (table.go:159,171). `updateImageTable()` (table.go:206) calls `m.imageTable.SetItems(m.imageRows())`. `imageColumns()` (table.go:107) has no "pulling"/status column beyond the existing "Scanned" column — a pull indicator would need either reusing that pattern (add `Pulling bool` to `imageRow`, decorate a cell) or piggy-backing on the existing scan-style column.
- Refresh mechanism: `fetchImages()` (commands.go:35) calls `docker.ListImages()`, returning `ImagesListMsg`; it's invoked on a 10s poll (`tickCmd`/`RefreshTickMsg`, commands.go:25-32) and explicitly after actions, e.g. `handleRegistryPullComplete` (browser_bridge.go:74-85) already does `tea.Batch(fetchImages(), m.footer.Info(...))` after a successful pull today. So a freshly-pulled image does appear after refresh — no extra plumbing needed there, but note: **a brand-new image tag has no row until that `fetchImages()` result lands**, so a pull-spinner on an "images row" only works for a name/tag already present in `m.images` at the time `G` is pressed; a wholly new tag would need a synthesized placeholder row or would simply appear un-spun once the list refreshes.
- Entry points to wire: `browser_tags.go:116` `pullSelectedTag()` (sets `b.operation="pull"`, `b.state = browserStateStatus`, calls `pullRegistryImageCmd(name)`) and `commands.go:574` `pullRegistryImageCmd(imageName) tea.Cmd` (calls `docker.PullImage`, returns `RegistryPullCompleteMsg{ImageName, Err}` — commands.go:576, model.go:275-276). This message is *not* currently a `jobs.Reporter`/routed via `routeWork`; it's handled directly by `handleRegistryPullComplete` (browser_bridge.go:74) via the normal `update.go:182` case, since `docker.PullImage` (internal/docker/images.go:227) is a single synchronous call with no starting/finished pair yet — a "starting" transition would need to be introduced (mirroring `ImageScanStartingMsg`/`Cancel`) to get the `ItemRunning` state jobs.Cancellable() needs.</result>

## Report: Images table pull-spinner investigation

**1. Model/row definition**

- `Model` (top-level struct): `internal/ui/oci_resources/model.go:31-102`. Images-tab fields: `images []docker.Image` (35), `imageTable datatable.Model[imageRow]` (48), `jobs []jobs.Run` / `jobFrame string` (44-45), `scanCache`, `failedScans`.
- Row type `imageRow`: `internal/ui/oci_resources/table.go:27-36` — `Image docker.Image`, `DisplayName`, `RawName`, `Entry cache.ImageScanEntry`, `Scanned/Scanning/Failed bool`, `SpinnerFrame string`. All `Cell` funcs return plain strings (Rule 122), e.g. `scannedCell` (table.go:92-102) returns `r.SpinnerFrame + "scanning"`; color comes from `Style` funcs like `scannedStyle` (table.go:79-88). `imageColumns()` at table.go:107-150; `imageColumnID = 0` is reserved as the row's status/busy cell (table.go:41-43, comment 368-375 in model.go).

**2. Refresh mechanism**

- `fetchImages()` Cmd: `internal/ui/oci_resources/commands.go:35-40`, calls `docker.ListImages()`, returns `ImagesListMsg{Images, Err}` (model.go:129-132).
- Triggers: on view `Init()` (update.go:20), and every 10s via `tickCmd()`/`RefreshTickMsg` (`commands.go:25-31`, handled at `update.go:77-78`, which re-fires `fetchImages()`).
- Result handled by `handleImagesList` (`results.go:70-80`), which sets `m.images` and calls `m.updateImageTable()`.
- `updateImageTable()` (table.go:206-209) rebuilds rows via `imageRows()` (table.go:153-177) and calls `imageTable.SetItems`.

**3. Existing per-row busy/spinner concepts (two distinct mechanisms, both usable as templates)**

- **Delete busy marker** (closest template): `datatable.Model[T]` has built-in `MarkBusy(key, label)`/`ClearBusy(key)`/`IsBusy(key)` (`internal/ui/datatable/datatable.go:556-583`) plus `AdvanceSpinner()`/`BusyLabels()` (600-605, 588-598). "Busy wins over state" is baked into the table's own render (`busyLabel`, datatable.go:607-614) — no per-column Style wiring needed in the view. Used for image delete: `results.go:24` `m.imageTable.MarkBusy(img.ID, "Removing "+name)`, cleared at `results.go:96` `m.imageTable.ClearBusy(msg.ID)`. Frame advance happens in `busy.go:31-37` `advanceBusySpinners()`, called from the `spinner.TickMsg` case in `update.go:56`.
- **Scan spinner** (job-registry driven, matches what you cited from browser_view.go's pattern): `imageRow.Scanning`/`SpinnerFrame` are set in `imageRows()` (table.go:159,171,173) from `m.scanningNames()` (`jobs.go:73-86`) and `m.jobFrame` (set in `handleJobsChanged`, `jobs.go:26-38`, driven by the central `internal/jobs` registry's `jobs.ChangedMsg`, handled at `update.go:48-49`). `ImageScanStartingMsg`/`ImageScanFinishedMsg` implement `jobs.Reporter` via `Transition()` (`jobs.go:95-106`), fed through `jobs.Start(run, cmd)` (e.g. `images.go:68-71`). Note `jobs.KindPull` already exists in `internal/jobs/jobs.go:33` (`Verb()`→"Pulling", `Cancellable()`→true at line 64) but is **currently unused anywhere** — the registry-browser pull does not go through `jobs.Start`/the router at all.

**4. How a pulled image becomes visible**

No explicit refresh-on-pull-complete hook exists structurally distinct from the generic mechanism — it's explicit but simple: `handleRegistryPullComplete` (`browser_bridge.go:74-85`) on success calls `m.registryBrowser.SetOperationSuccess()` then returns `tea.Batch(fetchImages(), m.footer.Info("Image pulled: "+msg.ImageName))` (line 84). So the table is refreshed immediately on pull completion (not waiting for the 10s tick), by explicitly invoking `fetchImages()`.

**5. Browser → parent message path**

- `RegistryPullCompleteMsg{ImageName, Err}` (model.go:276-279) is emitted by `pullRegistryImageCmd(imageName)` (`commands.go:574-579`) after `docker.PullImage`.
- The pull is launched from `RegistryBrowser.pullSelectedTag()` (`browser_tags.go:116-128`), invoked on key `keymap.Get` ("G") inside `browser_keys.go:214-215`. This is browser-local state: sets `b.imageName`, `b.operation = "pull"`, `b.state = browserStateStatus`, returns `tea.Batch(b.spinner.Tick, pullRegistryImageCmd(name))` — no `jobs.Start`, no marker on `Model.imageTable`.
- The parent's `Update()` routes `RegistryPullCompleteMsg` directly (not through the browser sub-update) at `update.go:182` → `handleRegistryPullComplete` (`browser_bridge.go:74-85`), which is exactly where `Model.imageTable` and `Model.images` live, so this is the natural interception point.
- **Gap for the planned feature**: there's currently no message fired at *pull start* that reaches the parent `Model` (only completion does, via `RegistryPullCompleteMsg`). To mark a row "pulling" while the pull runs, `pullSelectedTag()` (browser_tags.go:116) would need to also emit something the parent's `Update()` switch (`update.go`) can catch before/alongside entering `browserStateStatus`, e.g. a new `RegistryPullStartingMsg{ImageName}` propagated up (mirroring `ImageScanStartingMsg`), since currently only the browser's *own* status screen shows pull progress — the parent Images table has no visibility into an in-flight pull at all.
- Caveat: `imageTable`'s `Key` is `img.ID` (model.go:367), but a freshly-requested pull has no local image/ID yet — if the target image name doesn't already exist as a local row (e.g. new tag), `MarkBusy`-by-ID can't target it until after `fetchImages()` returns. A name-keyed marker (parallel structure to `m.failedScans map[string]bool`, keyed on image name/`RawName`) would be needed rather than reusing `imageTable.MarkBusy(id, ...)` directly, unless the image is already present locally (e.g. re-pulling an existing tag).</result>

- `Model` (top-level struct): `internal/ui/oci_resources/model.go:31-102`. Images-tab fields: `images []docker.Image` (35), `imageTable datatable.Model[imageRow]` (48), `jobs []jobs.Run` / `jobFrame string` (44-45), `scanCache`, `failedScans`.
- Row type `imageRow`: `internal/ui/oci_resources/table.go:27-36` — `Image docker.Image`, `DisplayName`, `RawName`, `Entry cache.ImageScanEntry`, `Scanned/Scanning/Failed bool`, `SpinnerFrame string`. All `Cell` funcs return plain strings (Rule 122), e.g. `scannedCell` (table.go:92-102) returns `r.SpinnerFrame + "scanning"`; color comes from `Style` funcs like `scannedStyle` (table.go:79-88). `imageColumns()` at table.go:107-150; `imageColumnID = 0` is reserved as the row's status/busy cell (table.go:41-43, comment 368-375 in model.go).

**2. Refresh mechanism**

- `fetchImages()` Cmd: `internal/ui/oci_resources/commands.go:35-40`, calls `docker.ListImages()`, returns `ImagesListMsg{Images, Err}` (model.go:129-132).
- Triggers: on view `Init()` (update.go:20), and every 10s via `tickCmd()`/`RefreshTickMsg` (`commands.go:25-31`, handled at `update.go:77-78`, which re-fires `fetchImages()`).
- Result handled by `handleImagesList` (`results.go:70-80`), which sets `m.images` and calls `m.updateImageTable()`.
- `updateImageTable()` (table.go:206-209) rebuilds rows via `imageRows()` (table.go:153-177) and calls `imageTable.SetItems`.

**3. Existing per-row busy/spinner concepts (two distinct mechanisms, both usable as templates)**

- **Delete busy marker** (closest template): `datatable.Model[T]` has built-in `MarkBusy(key, label)`/`ClearBusy(key)`/`IsBusy(key)` (`internal/ui/datatable/datatable.go:556-583`) plus `AdvanceSpinner()`/`BusyLabels()` (600-605, 588-598). "Busy wins over state" is baked into the table's own render (`busyLabel`, datatable.go:607-614) — no per-column Style wiring needed in the view. Used for image delete: `results.go:24` `m.imageTable.MarkBusy(img.ID, "Removing "+name)`, cleared at `results.go:96` `m.imageTable.ClearBusy(msg.ID)`. Frame advance happens in `busy.go:31-37` `advanceBusySpinners()`, called from the `spinner.TickMsg` case in `update.go:56`.
- **Scan spinner** (job-registry driven, matches what you cited from browser_view.go's pattern): `imageRow.Scanning`/`SpinnerFrame` are set in `imageRows()` (table.go:159,171,173) from `m.scanningNames()` (`jobs.go:73-86`) and `m.jobFrame` (set in `handleJobsChanged`, `jobs.go:26-38`, driven by the central `internal/jobs` registry's `jobs.ChangedMsg`, handled at `update.go:48-49`). `ImageScanStartingMsg`/`ImageScanFinishedMsg` implement `jobs.Reporter` via `Transition()` (`jobs.go:95-106`), fed through `jobs.Start(run, cmd)` (e.g. `images.go:68-71`). Note `jobs.KindPull` already exists in `internal/jobs/jobs.go:33` (`Verb()`→"Pulling", `Cancellable()`→true at line 64) but is **currently unused anywhere** — the registry-browser pull does not go through `jobs.Start`/the router at all.

**4. How a pulled image becomes visible**

No explicit refresh-on-pull-complete hook exists structurally distinct from the generic mechanism — it's explicit but simple: `handleRegistryPullComplete` (`browser_bridge.go:74-85`) on success calls `m.registryBrowser.SetOperationSuccess()` then returns `tea.Batch(fetchImages(), m.footer.Info("Image pulled: "+msg.ImageName))` (line 84). So the table is refreshed immediately on pull completion (not waiting for the 10s tick), by explicitly invoking `fetchImages()`.

**5. Browser → parent message path**

- `RegistryPullCompleteMsg{ImageName, Err}` (model.go:276-279) is emitted by `pullRegistryImageCmd(imageName)` (`commands.go:574-579`) after `docker.PullImage`.
- The pull is launched from `RegistryBrowser.pullSelectedTag()` (`browser_tags.go:116-128`), invoked on key `keymap.Get` ("G") inside `browser_keys.go:214-215`. This is browser-local state: sets `b.imageName`, `b.operation = "pull"`, `b.state = browserStateStatus`, returns `tea.Batch(b.spinner.Tick, pullRegistryImageCmd(name))` — no `jobs.Start`, no marker on `Model.imageTable`.
- The parent's `Update()` routes `RegistryPullCompleteMsg` directly (not through the browser sub-update) at `update.go:182` → `handleRegistryPullComplete` (`browser_bridge.go:74-85`), which is exactly where `Model.imageTable` and `Model.images` live, so this is the natural interception point.
- **Gap for the planned feature**: there's currently no message fired at *pull start* that reaches the parent `Model` (only completion does, via `RegistryPullCompleteMsg`). To mark a row "pulling" while the pull runs, `pullSelectedTag()` (browser_tags.go:116) would need to also emit something the parent's `Update()` switch (`update.go`) can catch before/alongside entering `browserStateStatus`, e.g. a new `RegistryPullStartingMsg{ImageName}` propagated up (mirroring `ImageScanStartingMsg`), since currently only the browser's *own* status screen shows pull progress — the parent Images table has no visibility into an in-flight pull at all.
- Caveat: `imageTable`'s `Key` is `img.ID` (model.go:367), but a freshly-requested pull has no local image/ID yet — if the target image name doesn't already exist as a local row (e.g. new tag), `MarkBusy`-by-ID can't target it until after `fetchImages()` returns. A name-keyed marker (parallel structure to `m.failedScans map[string]bool`, keyed on image name/`RawName`) would be needed rather than reusing `imageTable.MarkBusy(id, ...)` directly, unless the image is already present locally (e.g. re-pulling an existing tag).</result>

questions.question: Un pull concerne souvent une image jamais vue localement (c'est le but de la parcourir dans le registre). La table oci/images doit-elle alors afficher une ligne temporaire (placeholder) avec le spinner pendant que l'image n'existe pas encore localement, ou le spinner ne doit-il apparaître que si l'image est déjà listée (re-pull d'une image existante) ?

options.label: Ligne placeholder (Recommandé)
options.description: Une ligne apparaît immédiatement dans la table avec le spinner "Pulling", même pour une image jamais pull. Elle est remplacée par la vraie ligne dès que le pull se termine et que la liste se rafraîchit. Couvre le cas d'usage principal (parcourir puis pull) mais demande un peu plus de travail (clé synthétique, ligne de remplacement).

options.label: Spinner seulement si déjà locale
options.description: Plus simple : si l'image cible n'a pas encore de ligne locale, rien ne s'affiche pendant le pull — elle apparaît d'un coup une fois terminée. Le cas "nouvelle image" (le plus fréquent en pratique) n'a alors pas de retour visuel dans la table.

questions.question: Le pull doit-il pouvoir être annulé avec K pendant qu'il tourne (comme les autres jobs de §3.58) ? `docker.PullImage` utilise aujourd'hui exec.Command sans contexte annulable — le support K demanderait de le faire passer à exec.CommandContext.

options.label: Hors scope pour ce plan (Recommandé)
options.description: Le pull est enregistré comme job (visible dans :jobs, spinner partagé) mais K n'est pas câblé dessus cette fois — c'est un suivi naturel étant donné que jobs.KindPull.Cancellable() vaut déjà true.

options.label: Inclure l'annulation K maintenant
options.description: Modifier docker.PullImage pour accepter un contexte annulable et câbler K dans oci_resources pour arrêter un pull en cours, en plus du job + spinner.

1	// Package jobs holds what the application knows about work that outlives the
2	// moment it was started: a scan, a sync, a clone, a pull, a delete.
3	//
4	// Before it, four bookkeepings ran in parallel and none could see the others —
5	// workspaces kept three maps of paths, oci_resources a map of image names, the
6	// security inventory a flag per row, and the clone screen five states per
7	// repository. A scan started from `:sec` was therefore invisible to the `busy()`
8	// guard in `ws`, and the two wrote the same cache entry. Each of them also
9	// stamped its own spinner frame, which is four chains to keep alive and four
10	// ways for one to die unnoticed.
11	//
12	// The registry is owned by the router and read by the views through a snapshot
13	// carried in a message — never through a shared pointer. See D1 in
14	// .claude/plans/jobs-registry.plan.md for why, and internal/app/jobs.go for the
15	// broadcast.
16	package jobs
17	
18	import (
19		"context"
20		"time"
21	
22		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/command"
23	)
24	
25	// Kind is what a run does. It decides the icon, the footer verb and — at
26	// poste 8 — whether the run can be cancelled at all.
27	type Kind string
28	
29	const (
30		KindScan   Kind = "scan"
31		KindSync   Kind = "sync"
32		KindClone  Kind = "clone"
33		KindPull   Kind = "pull"
34		KindCreate Kind = "create"
35		KindDelete Kind = "delete"
36	)
37	
38	// Kinds returns every declared kind, in the order a view should offer them.
39	// It exists to be walked by a test: a kind without an icon or without a verb
40	// is a hole that only shows up on the screen that needed it.
41	func Kinds() []Kind {
42		return []Kind{KindScan, KindSync, KindClone, KindPull, KindCreate, KindDelete}
43	}
44	
45	// Cancellable reports whether stopping a run of this kind leaves the machine in
46	// a state the user asked for.
47	//
48	// The queue always stops — nothing further starts, whatever the kind — so this
49	// answers the narrower question of whether work already in flight can be cut.
50	// It is the table from D7, kept next to the kinds so a new kind cannot be added
51	// without answering it:
52	//
53	//	scan    yes  Trivy and Gitleaks read; cutting leaves nothing behind
54	//	pull    yes  a docker pull resumes by layer
55	//	sync    no   the queue stops, a fast-forward in flight is waited out
56	//	clone   no   a cut git clone leaves half a repository on disk
57	//	create  no   a request already sent cannot be un-sent
58	//	delete  no   half deleted is worse than deleted
59	//
60	// A run whose kind answers no still accepts Cancel: the queue stopping is worth
61	// having on its own. What the answer gates is whether a view offers the key on
62	// a single item (Rule 130 — greyed, with a named reason, never silent).
63	func (k Kind) Cancellable() bool {
64		return k == KindScan || k == KindPull
65	}
66	
67	// Verb is what a kind is called while it runs — present participle, English US
68	// (Rule 129). It lives here rather than in a view because two now say it: the
69	// footer of the view that launched the run, and the `:jobs` list.
70	//
71	// A kind that reaches the default is a kind added without answering this, which
72	// is what walking Kinds() in a test catches.
73	func (k Kind) Verb() string {
74		switch k {
75		case KindScan:
76			return "Scanning"
77		case KindSync:
78			return "Syncing"
79		case KindClone:
80			return "Cloning"
81		case KindPull:
82			return "Pulling"
83		case KindCreate:
84			return "Creating"
85		case KindDelete:
86			return "Deleting"
87		}
88		return "Working"
89	}
90	
91	// ItemState is where one target stands.
92	//
93	// queued and running are distinguished on purpose (D6): the semaphore already
94	// knows the difference, the clone screen already shows it, and "4 running, 8
95	// waiting" is the one sentence a jobs view exists to say. Collapsing them would
96	// make the clone screen the only honest view in the application.
97	type ItemState string
98	
99	const (
100		ItemQueued  ItemState = "queued"
101		ItemRunning ItemState = "running"
102		ItemDone    ItemState = "done"
103		ItemSkipped ItemState = "skipped"
104		ItemFailed  ItemState = "failed"
105	)
106	
107	// Terminal reports whether the state is one the item will not leave.
108	func (s ItemState) Terminal() bool {
109		return s == ItemDone || s == ItemSkipped || s == ItemFailed
110	}
111	
112	// RunState is derived from the items, never stored. A field would be a second
113	// source of truth for a question the items already answer, and the two would
114	// drift the first time a transition was missed.
115	type RunState string
116	
117	const (
118		RunQueued    RunState = "queued"
119		RunRunning   RunState = "running"
120		RunDone      RunState = "done"
121		RunFailed    RunState = "failed"
122		RunCancelled RunState = "cancelled"
123	)
124	
125	// JobID identifies a run for the life of the session.
126	type JobID int
127	
128	// Item is one target inside a run: a repository path, an image reference, a
129	// group path.
130	type Item struct {
131		// Target is the identity transitions are addressed to, and it is unique
132		// within a run.
133		Target string
134		// Display is what a view shows — a registry alias applied, a path
135		// shortened. Empty means "show the target".
136		Display string
137		State   ItemState
138		// Detail carries what the state alone cannot say: "already there", the
139		// reason a scan failed.
140		Detail string
141	
142		// cancel is unexported and deliberately does not travel: Snapshot clears it
143		// on the copies it hands out, so a view holding a snapshot cannot stop a job
144		// behind the router's back. Cancelling goes through Registry.Cancel, which
145		// the owner runs — the same asymmetry as the snapshot itself (D1).
146		cancel context.CancelFunc
147	}
148	
149	// Name returns what a view should print for the item.
150	func (i Item) Name() string {
151		if i.Display != "" {
152			return i.Display
153		}
154		return i.Target
155	}
156	
157	// Run is one batch of work, started in one go from one view.
158	type Run struct {
159		ID   JobID
160		Kind Kind
161		// Origin is the view that started the run: where `:jobs` sends the user
162		// back, and what decides whether a footer keeps its detailed line (D9).
163		Origin command.ViewType
164		// Context is stamped at launch and never re-read. It is what lets `:jobs`
165		// filter on the current context instead of purging on a switch — which
166		// would contradict keeping runs for the session (D8) — and it is what stops
167		// a batch outliving a context switch from writing its results into the
168		// wrong cache.
169		Context string
170		// Label names the run for a human: "~/work/perso", "nexus.example.com/team".
171		Label     string
172		Items     []Item
173		StartedAt time.Time
174		EndedAt   time.Time
175	
176		// cancelled records that someone asked for this run to stop. Without it a
177		// cancelled run reads as done once its items settle, and a jobs view that
178		// cannot tell "finished" from "you stopped it" is missing the one fact the
179		// user is looking for.
180		cancelled bool
181	
182		// open says the target list is still being discovered (D3). An open run is
183		// never finished, however its items stand: a clone whose walk has found
184		// three repositories and cloned all three is not done — the walk is still
185		// going, and settling it there would stop the spinner chain and print a
186		// summary the next repository contradicts.
187		//
188		// Every other kind knows its full list when it is admitted, which is what
189		// makes "8 waiting" sayable at all (D10). The clone is the exception
190		// because its walk *is* the work that finds them.
191		open bool
192	
193		// cancel stops the run's queue. Cleared by Snapshot, like Item.cancel.
194		cancel context.CancelFunc
195	}
196	
197	// NewRun builds a run with every target queued. StartedAt is left to the
198	// registry, which stamps it when the run is admitted.
199	func NewRun(kind Kind, origin command.ViewType, contextName, label string, targets ...string) Run {
200		items := make([]Item, len(targets))
201		for i, target := range targets {
202			items[i] = Item{Target: target, State: ItemQueued}
203		}
204		return Run{
205			Kind:    kind,
206			Origin:  origin,
207			Context: contextName,
208			Label:   label,
209			Items:   items,
210		}
211	}
212	
213	// NewOpenRun builds a run whose targets are not known yet.
214	//
215	// It is the clone's shape and only the clone's: the walk that discovers
216	// repositories is itself the slow part, so a run that waited for the full list
217	// would show nothing for the minutes that matter. Targets arrive through
218	// Registry.Discover, and Registry.Seal says there will be no more.
219	func NewOpenRun(kind Kind, origin command.ViewType, contextName, label string) Run {
220		return Run{
221			Kind:    kind,
222			Origin:  origin,
223			Context: contextName,
224			Label:   label,
225			open:    true,
226		}
227	}
228	
229	// Open reports whether the run is still discovering its targets.
230	func (r Run) Open() bool { return r.open }
231	
232	// WithDisplay names how one target should be printed. It is separate from
233	// NewRun because only some kinds have one — an image reference goes through a
234	// registry alias, a repository path does not.
235	func (r Run) WithDisplay(target, display string) Run {
236		items := make([]Item, len(r.Items))
237		copy(items, r.Items)
238		for i := range items {
239			if items[i].Target == target {
240				items[i].Display = display
241			}
242		}
243		r.Items = items
244		return r
245	}
246	
247	// State derives where the run stands from its items.
248	//
249	// The order of the three settled answers is the order in which they matter: a
250	// run that was cancelled reads cancelled even though its items failed for that
251	// very reason, and one failure is enough to make the whole run a failure.
252	func (r Run) State() RunState {
253		var running, terminal, failed int
254		for _, item := range r.Items {
255			switch {
256			case item.State == ItemRunning:
257				running++
258			case item.State.Terminal():
259				terminal++
260				if item.State == ItemFailed {
261					failed++
262				}
263			}
264		}
265	
266		// An open run is unsettled whatever its items say: more of them are coming.
267		if r.open || terminal < len(r.Items) {
268			if running > 0 || terminal > 0 {
269				return RunRunning
270			}
271			return RunQueued
272		}
273	
274		switch {
275		case r.cancelled:
276			return RunCancelled
277		case failed > 0:
278			return RunFailed
279		default:
280			return RunDone
281		}
282	}
283	
284	// Finished reports whether every item has settled. An empty *sealed* run is
285	// finished: there is nothing left for it to do, and reporting it as running
286	// would leave the spinner chain alive forever. An empty *open* one is not — it
287	// has found nothing yet, which is where every clone starts.
288	func (r Run) Finished() bool {
289		state := r.State()
290		return state != RunRunning && state != RunQueued
291	}
292	
293	// Cancelled reports whether the run was asked to stop, whether or not its items
294	// have settled yet.
295	func (r Run) Cancelled() bool { return r.cancelled }
296	
297	// Total is the first half of the "3/12" a footer prints.
298	func (r Run) Total() int { return len(r.Items) }
299	
300	// Done is the second half. Both are derived rather than counted alongside,
301	// which is what removes the need for a scanRun struct beside the existing
302	// syncRun — the two were the same pair of integers maintained by hand.
303	//
304	// It counts the items that have settled, whichever way they settled: a skipped
305	// repository and a failed one are both finished with, which is what a progress
306	// line reports on.
307	func (r Run) Done() int {
308		n := 0
309		for _, item := range r.Items {
310			if item.State.Terminal() {
311				n++
312			}
313		}
314		return n
315	}
316	
317	// Stoppable reports whether asking this run to stop would change anything.
318	//
319	// It is D7 read as a question about *this* run rather than about its kind,
320	// which is what a view needs to decide whether to offer the key (Rule 130):
321	//
322	//   - a settled run has nothing left to stop;
323	//   - a kind whose work can be cut always has something — whatever is in flight;
324	//   - a run still discovering has its walk to stop, even with nothing queued;
325	//   - anything else can still have its queue stopped, if there is a queue.
326	//
327	// A delete falls through all four while it runs: one item, in flight, of a kind
328	// that must never be cut. That is the case the key is greyed for, and it is the
329	// reason this is a method rather than `!Finished()`. A create answers the same
330	// way and for the same reason.
331	func (r Run) Stoppable() bool {
332		switch {
333		case r.Finished():
334			return false
335		case r.Kind.Cancellable(), r.open:
336			return true
337		}
338		for _, item := range r.Items {
339			if item.State == ItemQueued {
340				return true
341			}
342		}
343		return false
344	}
345	
346	// ItemStoppable reports whether one target can be stopped on its own.
347	//
348	// Narrower than Stoppable on purpose: stopping the run stops its queue whatever
349	// the kind, but cutting one target in flight is only offered where cutting
350	// leaves nothing behind (Kind.Cancellable). A half-written clone is the case
351	// that decides it.
352	func (r Run) ItemStoppable(item Item) bool {
353		return !item.State.Terminal() && r.Kind.Cancellable()
354	}
355	
356	// Counts returns how many items sit in each state, for a view that wants to say
357	// more than "3/12".
358	func (r Run) Counts() map[ItemState]int {
359		out := make(map[ItemState]int, 5)
360		for _, item := range r.Items {
361			out[item.State]++
362		}
363		return out
364	}
365	
366	// FilterContext keeps the runs stamped with the given context.
367	//
368	// It is a function over a snapshot rather than a second registry method: the
369	// snapshot is what travels in the message, so this is where every view that
370	// needs the filter already has the data (D8).
371	func FilterContext(runs []Run, contextName string) []Run {
372		out := make([]Run, 0, len(runs))
373		for _, run := range runs {
374			if run.Context == contextName {
375				out = append(out, run)
376			}
377		}
378		return out
379	}
380	
381	// Unfinished keeps the runs that are still going.
382	func Unfinished(runs []Run) []Run {
383		out := make([]Run, 0, len(runs))
384		for _, run := range runs {
385			if !run.Finished() {
386				out = append(out, run)
387			}
388		}
389		return out
390	}

261	// Cancel asks a run to stop.
262	//
263	// What that means differs by kind, and the difference is not cosmetic (D7):
264	// the queue always stops, so nothing further starts, but work already in flight
265	// is only interrupted where interrupting it leaves nothing behind. A `git
266	// clone` is never cut — a cancelled one leaves half a repository on disk — and
267	// a delete is not cancellable at all, which is a guard the view carries
268	// (Kind.Cancellable).
269	//
270	// Queued items are marked skipped straight away: they will not run, and leaving
271	// them queued would keep the run reading as running forever.
272	func (r *Registry) Cancel(id JobID) bool {
273		run := r.run(id)
274		if run == nil || run.Finished() {
275			return false
276		}
277	
278		run.cancelled = true
279		// A cancelled walk finds nothing more, so the run is sealed here: leaving
280		// it open would keep it unsettled for the life of the session, spinner
281		// chain and all, with nothing left that could ever close it.
282		run.open = false
283		if run.cancel != nil {
284			run.cancel()
285			run.cancel = nil
286		}
287	
288		for i := range run.Items {
289			switch run.Items[i].State {
290			case ItemQueued:
291				run.Items[i].State = ItemSkipped
292				run.Items[i].Detail = "cancelled"
293			case ItemRunning:
294				// Asked to stop, not declared stopped: the item reports its own
295				// outcome when it gets there. Claiming it settled here would race
296				// the message that says how it actually ended.
297				if run.Items[i].cancel != nil {
298					run.Items[i].cancel()
299					run.Items[i].cancel = nil
300				}
301			}
302		}
303	
304		r.settle(run)
305		return true
306	}
307	
308	// CancelItem stops one target of a run, leaving the rest going.
309	//
310	// It is the narrow half of D7: the run-level Cancel stops the queue whatever
311	// the kind, and this cuts a single piece of work — which is only offered where
312	// cutting leaves nothing behind. The caller decides that (Run.ItemStoppable);
313	// this refuses only what it cannot do.
314	//
315	// A queued target is skipped outright, because it will not run. A running one
316	// is *asked* to stop and left running: it reports its own outcome when it gets
317	// there, and claiming it settled here would race the message that says how it
318	// actually ended — the same reason Cancel gives.
319	func (r *Registry) CancelItem(id JobID, target string) bool {
320		run := r.run(id)
321		if run == nil || run.Finished() {
322			return false
323		}
324		for i := range run.Items {
325			if run.Items[i].Target != target || run.Items[i].State.Terminal() {
326				continue
327			}
328			if run.Items[i].State == ItemQueued {
329				run.Items[i].State = ItemSkipped
330				run.Items[i].Detail = "cancelled"
331			} else if run.Items[i].cancel != nil {
332				run.Items[i].cancel()
333				run.Items[i].cancel = nil
334			}
335			r.settle(run)
336			return true
337		}
338		return false
339	}

18	// imageRow is one line of the Images tab: the image, plus everything the row
19	// says about it that does not live on the image — the cached scan counts,
20	// whether a scan is running or the last one failed, and the alias-substituted
21	// name.
22	//
23	// The columns are built once, in New, so their Cell functions cannot reach back
24	// into the model for any of that. Carrying it on the row instead is what keeps
25	// the sort honest: the C column orders by the same number it prints, where the
26	// old comparator looked the entry up a second time.
27	type imageRow struct {
28		Image        docker.Image
29		DisplayName  string
30		RawName      string
31		Entry        cache.ImageScanEntry
32		Scanned      bool
33		Scanning     bool
34		Failed       bool
35		SpinnerFrame string
36	}
37	
38	// The columns something else refers to. imageColumnID is where a running action
39	// puts its spinner; imageColumnName is what the tab opens sorted by.
40	const (
41		imageColumnID   = 0
42		imageColumnName = 1
43	)
44	
45	// secretsColumnWidth is the Secrets column, at the width the workspaces list
46	// gives it. Elle ne trie pas, comme là-bas : `datatable` réserve deux cellules
47	// de plus à une colonne triable pour sa flèche, ce qui est cher pour un glyphe.
48	const secretsColumnWidth = 7
49	
50	// secrets is the row's verdict — inconnu tant que l'image n'a pas été scannée,
51	// et inconnu aussi pour un scan qui n'a pas eu d'étape secrets.
52	func (r imageRow) secrets() theme.SecretsState {
53		return theme.SecretsVerdict(r.Entry.Sensitive, r.Scanned)
54	}
55	
56	// cveColumn builds one of the four severity count columns.
57	//
58	// severity names the column's level for the colour, spelled as the scanners
59	// spell it — the title here is a single letter, which is no basis for deciding
60	// what colour a count is.
61	func cveColumn(title, severity string, get func(cache.ImageScanEntry) int) datatable.Column[imageRow] {
62		return datatable.Column[imageRow]{
63			Title: title, Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 4,
64			Cell: func(r imageRow) string { return formatCVECount(get(r.Entry), r.Scanned) },
65			// A zero is dim, like an unscanned image: four coloured zeroes on a
66			// clean image would read as four findings.
67			Style: func(r imageRow) lipgloss.Style {
68				if !r.Scanned || get(r.Entry) == 0 {
69					return theme.DimStyle
70				}
71				return theme.SeverityTextStyle(severity)
72			},
73			Less: func(a, b imageRow) bool { return get(a.Entry) < get(b.Entry) },
74		}
75	}
76	
77	// scannedStyle colours the scan state, a failure being the one value in the
78	// column that asks for anything.
79	func scannedStyle(r imageRow) lipgloss.Style {
80		switch {
81		case r.Failed:
82			return theme.StatusErrorStyle
83		case r.Scanning, !r.Scanned:
84			return theme.DimStyle
85		}
86		// Aucune opinion : c'est la table qui pose la couleur de texte du thème.
87		return lipgloss.NewStyle()
88	}
89	
90	// scannedCell reports the scan state: the spinner while one runs, an error icon
91	// when the last attempt failed, otherwise how long ago it succeeded.
92	func scannedCell(r imageRow) string {
93		switch {
94		case r.Scanning:
95			return r.SpinnerFrame + "scanning"
96		case r.Failed:
97			return theme.IconError + " error"
98		case r.Scanned:
99			return timeAgo(r.Entry.ScannedAt)
100		}
101		return "-"
102	}
103	
104	// imageColumns describes the Images tab. ID is the only column that neither
105	// sorts nor searches — twelve hex characters are not something anyone orders or
106	// looks for.
107	func imageColumns() []datatable.Column[imageRow] {
108		return []datatable.Column[imageRow]{
109			{
110				Title: "ID", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 14,
111				Cell: func(r imageRow) string { return shortID(r.Image.ID) },
112			},
113			{
114				Title: "Name", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent,
115				MinWidth: 20, MaxWidth: 48, Flex: 1, TruncateHead: true,
116				Cell: func(r imageRow) string { return r.DisplayName },
117				Less: func(a, b imageRow) bool { return strings.ToLower(a.RawName) < strings.ToLower(b.RawName) },
118				// Both names. The filter has always matched the repository and tag
119				// docker reports; the alias the row actually shows was not
120				// searchable, which is a small thing that reads as a bug when the
121				// column says one name and the query wants the other.
122				Search: func(r imageRow) string { return r.DisplayName + " " + r.RawName },
123			},
124			{
125				Title: "Disk Usage", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 12,
126				Cell: func(r imageRow) string { return formatBytes(r.Image.UniqueSize) },
127				Less: func(a, b imageRow) bool { return a.Image.UniqueSize < b.Image.UniqueSize },
128			},
129			{
130				Title: "Content Size", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 14,
131				Cell: func(r imageRow) string { return formatBytes(r.Image.Size) },
132				Less: func(a, b imageRow) bool { return a.Image.Size < b.Image.Size },
133			},
134			{
135				Title: "Secrets", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: secretsColumnWidth,
136				Cell:  func(r imageRow) string { return theme.SecretsIcon(r.secrets()) },
137				Style: func(r imageRow) lipgloss.Style { return theme.SecretsStyle(r.secrets()) },
138			},
139			cveColumn("C", "CRITICAL", func(e cache.ImageScanEntry) int { return e.Critical }),
140			cveColumn("H", "HIGH", func(e cache.ImageScanEntry) int { return e.High }),
141			cveColumn("M", "MEDIUM", func(e cache.ImageScanEntry) int { return e.Medium }),
142			cveColumn("L", "LOW", func(e cache.ImageScanEntry) int { return e.Low }),
143			{
144				Title: "Scanned", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 14,
145				Cell:  scannedCell,

147				Less:  func(a, b imageRow) bool { return a.Entry.ScannedAt.Before(b.Entry.ScannedAt) },

152	// imageRows decorates the image list with the scan state the table shows.
153	func (m *Model) imageRows() []imageRow {
154		aliases := registryalias.From(m.registries)
155		// The scan frame comes from the registry, which holds the one chain that
156		// animates work (D5). spinnerFrameIdx below is local, and it animates
157		// loading — a load is not a job.
158		frame := m.jobFrame
159		scanning := m.scanningNames()

161		rows := make([]imageRow, 0, len(m.images))
162		for _, img := range m.images {

166				Image:        img,

171				Scanning:     scanning[raw],
172				Failed:       m.failedScans[raw],

179	// formatBytes formats bytes into human-readable string
180	func formatBytes(b int64) string {
181		switch {
182		case b >= 1e9:
183			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1f GB", float64(b)/1e9)
184		case b >= 1e6:
185			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1f MB", float64(b)/1e6)
186		case b >= 1e3:
187			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1f kB", float64(b)/1e3)
188		default:
189			return fmt.Sprintf("%d B", b)
190		}
191	}

193	// formatCVECount formats a CVE count for display, returns "-" if not scanned
194	func formatCVECount(count int, scanned bool) string {
195		if !scanned {
196			return "-"
197		}
198		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", count)
199	}
200	
201	// updateImageTable rebuilds the image table rows.
202	//
203	// Every caller reaches here after changing something the row shows — a scan
204	// started, finished, or the list came back — so the decoration is recomputed
205	// wholesale rather than patched in place.
206	func (m *Model) updateImageTable() {
207		m.imageTable.SetItems(m.imageRows())
208		m.imageTable.SetHeight(m.tableHeight())
209	}

211	// networkColumnID and volumeColumnDriver are where a running action puts its
212	// spinner — the cell each table can spare while one row is being removed.
213	const (
214		networkColumnID    = 0
215		volumeColumnDriver = 1
216	)
217	
218	// networkColumns describes the Networks tab. Neither this table nor the volumes
219	// one sorts or filters today, so no Less and no Search: `/` and `.` stay inert
220	// rather than being wired to a bar this view's footer does not render.
221	func networkColumns() []datatable.Column[docker.Network] {
222		return []datatable.Column[docker.Network]{
223			{Title: "ID", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 14, Cell: func(n docker.Network) string { return shortID(n.ID) }},
224			{Title: "Name", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 20, Flex: 1, Cell: func(n docker.Network) string { return n.Name }},
225			{Title: "Driver", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 12, Cell: func(n docker.Network) string { return n.Driver }},
226			{Title: "Scope", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 10, Cell: func(n docker.Network) string { return n.Scope }},
227		}
228	}
229	
230	// volumeColumns describes the Volumes tab.
231	func volumeColumns() []datatable.Column[docker.Volume] {
232		return []datatable.Column[docker.Volume]{
233			{Title: "Name", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 20, Cell: func(v docker.Volume) string { return v.Name }},
234			{Title: "Driver", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 12, Cell: func(v docker.Volume) string { return v.Driver }},
235			{Title: "Mountpoint", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, Optional: true, TruncateHead: true, MinWidth: 20, Flex: 1, Cell: func(v docker.Volume) string { return v.Mountpoint }},
236		}
237	}
238	
239	// shortID truncates a Docker ID to the twelve characters the CLI shows.
240	func shortID(id string) string {
241		if len(id) > 12 {
242			return id[:12]
243		}
244		return id
245	}
246	
247	// registryRow is one line of the Registries tab.
248	//
249	// The tab shows two populations in one table — the configured entries at the
250	// top level, and one group's discovered members after `→` — and datatable is
251	// generic over a single T, so the row type has to carry both. explorerRow
252	// exists for the same reason.
253	//
254	// config is the index into Model.registries the row stands for, and -1 for a
255	// discovered member: a member is not a config entry, has no alias of its own to
256	// edit and no credentials but its group's, so every action on the tab has to be
257	// able to tell the two apart. Carrying it on the row is also what lets the
258	// cursor be resolved without indexing m.registries by row number, which is
259	// correct today only because this table neither sorts nor filters.
260	type registryRow struct {
261		alias   string
262		url     string
263		kind    string
264		auth    string
265		logged  string
266		members string
267		config  int
268	}
269	
270	// registryColumnLogged is the cell a login or logout replaces with its spinner:
271	// it is precisely the answer the operation is about to change.
272	const registryColumnLogged = 4
273	
274	// registryColumns describes the Registries tab. Nothing sorts or searches: the
275	// list is the order the config declares, which is the order the user wrote.
276	func registryColumns() []datatable.Column[registryRow] {
277		return []datatable.Column[registryRow]{
278			{Title: "Alias", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 16, Cell: func(r registryRow) string { return r.alias }},
279			{Title: "URL", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, TruncateHead: true, MinWidth: 20, Flex: 1, Cell: func(r registryRow) string { return r.url }},
280			{Title: "Kind", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 10, Cell: func(r registryRow) string { return r.kind }},
281			{Title: "Auth", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 12, Cell: func(r registryRow) string { return r.auth }}, // holds "credentials"
282			{Title: "Logged", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 8, Cell: func(r registryRow) string { return r.logged }},
283			{Title: "Members", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 16, Cell: func(r registryRow) string { return r.members }}, // holds "12 · 30 days ago"
284		}
285	}
286	
287	// registryRef is what an entry is displayed as: its address, not its URL.
288	//
289	// The prefix has to be on screen or the tab says nothing useful — one line per
290	// proxy is one host repeated, and a group's members all answer to the same host
291	// too (§3.18). Joined with a slash because that is exactly the head of the pull
292	// reference: `docker pull nexus.example.com/dhi-io-proxy/eclipse-temurin:21`.
293	// Plain text only — Rule 122.
294	func registryRef(url, repoPrefix string) string {
295		if repoPrefix == "" {
296			return url
297		}
298		return strings.TrimSuffix(url, "/") + "/" + repoPrefix
299	}
300	
301	// membersCell reports what the last discovery for a group found, and when.
302	//
303	// The "when" is not decoration: a cache with no visible age is worse than the
304	// re-detection it replaced, because it looks current whatever it holds
305	// (§3.8, decision 3). Plain text only — Rule 122.
306	func (m *Model) membersCell(reg config.RegistryItem) string {
307		if reg.Kind != config.KindGroup {
308			return ""
309		}
310		if m.refreshingGroups[reg.Slug] {
311			// The spinner's frame, not its View(): the latter renders through a
312			// style, and a table cell carries no escape sequence.
313			return spinner.Dot.Frames[m.spinnerFrameIdx%len(spinner.Dot.Frames)] + " refreshing"
314		}
315		entry, ok := m.groupCache[reg.Slug]
316		if !ok {
317			return "never" // declared a group, never asked
318		}
319		return fmt.Sprintf("%d · %s", len(entry.Members), timeAgo(entry.DiscoveredAt))
320	}
321	
322	// loggedCell reports the docker login status for a registry URL.
323	func (m *Model) loggedCell(mode, url string) string {
324		if !config.UsesCredentials(mode) {
325			return "-"
326		}
327		if m.registryLoginStatus[url] {
328			return theme.IconOK
329		}
330		return theme.IconError
331	}
332	
333	// drilledGroup returns the group the tab has entered, or nil at the top level.
334	func (m *Model) drilledGroup() *config.RegistryItem {
335		if m.registryGroupSlug == "" {
336			return nil
337		}
338		for i := range m.registries {
339			if m.registries[i].Slug == m.registryGroupSlug {
340				return &m.registries[i]
341			}
342		}
343		return nil
344	}
345	
346	func (m *Model) updateRegistryTable() {
347		if group := m.drilledGroup(); group != nil {
348			m.updateGroupMemberTable(*group)
349			return
350		}
351		rows := make([]registryRow, 0, len(m.registries))
352		for i, reg := range m.registries {
353			rows = append(rows, registryRow{
354				alias:   reg.Alias,
355				url:     registryRef(reg.URL, reg.RepoPrefix),
356				kind:    reg.Kind,
357				auth:    reg.AuthMode,
358				logged:  m.loggedCell(reg.AuthMode, reg.URL),
359				members: m.membersCell(reg),
360				config:  i,
361			})
362		}
363		m.setRegistryRows(rows)
364	}
365	
366	// updateGroupMemberTable fills the table with one group's discovered members.
367	//
368	// A member is not a config entry: it has no alias of its own to edit, its
369	// credentials are the group's, and it is what the cache holds — so the columns
370	// say `inherit`, carry no member count, and the row points at no config entry.
371	func (m *Model) updateGroupMemberTable(group config.RegistryItem) {
372		entry := m.groupCache[group.Slug]
373		rows := make([]registryRow, 0, len(entry.Members))
374		for _, member := range entry.Members {
375			rows = append(rows, registryRow{
376				alias:  member.Alias,
377				url:    registryRef(member.URL, member.RepoPrefix),
378				kind:   "member",
379				auth:   config.AuthInherit,
380				logged: m.loggedCell(group.AuthMode, group.URL),
381				config: -1,
382			})
383		}
384		m.setRegistryRows(rows)
385	}
386	
387	func (m *Model) setRegistryRows(rows []registryRow) {
388		m.registryTable.SetItems(rows)
389		m.registryTable.Resize(m.width, m.tableHeight())
390	}

96	var footerMsgSeq atomic.Uint64
97	
98	// ClearFooterMsg expires the message identified by ID.
99	//
100	// The ID is what makes the type safe to share across packages. Two things would
101	// otherwise go wrong: a timer started by one view could clear the message of
102	// whichever view is active when it lands, and — the bug that was already
103	// present in all eight local implementations — a message set at t+2.9s was
104	// wiped at t+3s by its predecessor's timer.
105	type ClearFooterMsg struct{ ID uint64 }

109		text         string

113	}

115	// Info, Warn and Error set the message and return its expiry timer. Call them
116	// from Update() and return the Cmd — a message set without its timer never
117	// clears (Rule 128).
118	func (f *FooterMessage) Info(text string) tea.Cmd  { return f.set(text, LevelInfo) }
119	func (f *FooterMessage) Warn(text string) tea.Cmd  { return f.set(text, LevelWarning) }
120	func (f *FooterMessage) Error(text string) tea.Cmd { return f.set(text, LevelError) }

123		if text == "" {

1	package jobs
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5	
6		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
7	)
8	
9	// StartMsg asks the router to register a run and then dispatch the work that
10	// fills it.
11	//
12	// The view builds the run — it is the only place that knows the targets — and
13	// the router admits it, stamps it with the current context and starts the work
14	// (D10). Registration happens in Update, never inside a Cmd (Rule 110).
15	//
16	// Work rides on the message rather than being batched beside it because the
17	// order matters: a transition naming a run the registry has not admitted yet is
18	// refused, and a tea.Batch gives no order. The router is the sequencer, which
19	// is a smaller thing to get right than a Sequence at every launch site — and it
20	// leaves the work runnable only by the router, so a test can read what was
21	// launched without launching it.
22	type StartMsg struct {
23		Run Run
24	
25		// Work is a builder rather than a command because the context is stamped
26		// by the router, one step after the view has described the run (D8). Work
27		// that writes into a context-scoped cache needs that name, and reading it
28		// back from the configuration inside the command is the defect the stamp
29		// exists to close: a batch outliving a context switch wrote its last
30		// results into the cache of the context it had switched to.
31		//
32		// It is never nil for a run with work: Start passes a builder that ignores
33		// the name, so a launch site that has no use for it reads as it did.
34		Work func(contextName string) tea.Cmd
35	
36		// Cancel stops the run's queue, and is nil for the kinds that have nothing
37		// to stop. It travels here rather than arriving later like an item's cancel
38		// because a progressive run owns its context from the launch: the pipeline
39		// is started in Update, so the function exists before the run is admitted.
40		Cancel context.CancelFunc
41	}
42	
43	// Start builds the message for work that does not depend on the context.
44	func Start(run Run, work tea.Cmd) tea.Cmd {
45		return StartInContext(run, func(string) tea.Cmd { return work })
46	}
47	
48	// StartCancellable builds the message for a run whose queue can be stopped —
49	// today the clone, whose pipeline is launched from Update and hands back its
50	// context there and then.
51	func StartCancellable(run Run, work tea.Cmd, cancel context.CancelFunc) tea.Cmd {
52		return func() tea.Msg {
53			return StartMsg{
54				Run:    run,
55				Work:   func(string) tea.Cmd { return work },
56				Cancel: cancel,
57			}
58		}
59	}

379	security inventory a flag per row, and the clone screen five states per
380	repository. A scan started from `:sec` was therefore invisible to the `busy()`
381	guard in `ws`, and the two wrote the same cache entry.
382	
383	Two levels: a **`Run`** is one batch started in one go from one view, and holds
384	an **`Item`** per target. `RunState` is *derived* from the items and never
385	stored — a field would be a second answer to a question the items already
386	answer, and the two drift the first time a transition is missed.
387	
388	| | |
389	|---|---|
390	| `Start(run)` | admits a batch, from `Update` and never from a `Cmd` (Rule 110). Every launch site knows its full target list when it dispatches, which is what makes "8 waiting" sayable |
391	| `Advance(id, target, state, detail)` | one item moves. Returns false for work nobody registered, rather than swallowing it |
392	| `Attach` / `AttachRun` | store a `context.CancelFunc`; it arrives in the message that says the item started, because the context is created inside the `Cmd` |
393	| `Cancel(id)` | stops the queue always; cuts work in flight only where that leaves nothing behind (`Kind.Cancellable`) |
394	| `Snapshot()` | a **copy**, cancel functions cleared |
395	| `Running()` | runs that have not settled |
396	
397	`queued` and `running` are kept apart: the semaphore already knows the
398	difference and the clone screen already shows it, so collapsing them would make
399	that screen the only honest one.

402	are single-item runs against a forge, and they are registered for the three
403	things the registry gives that a local flag does not: the spinner frame comes
404	from the broadcast rather than from a view's own chain — the explorer's stops on
405	`!m.loading`, so a frame taken from it would freeze the moment the tree settled;
406	the `busy()` guard sees work started anywhere; and `Run.Context` is stamped at
407	launch, so a create that outlives a context switch cannot write into the tree it
408	switched to. What decides is whether the work is a network call the user has to
409	be told about, not how many targets it has.

411	Runs live for the session, capped at the last `MaxFinishedRuns` settled ones; a
412	run still going is never pruned. Each is stamped with the context it started in,
